DAMGHANI:v1p383/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r6.claim: Qaḍā can mean doing or carrying out an act, including carrying out God’s decree and the matter of marriage.
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r6.anchor: الرابع : قضى بمعنى فعل قوله تعالى في سورة طه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r7.claim: Pharaoh expected to awe ordinary magicians, but faced righteous believers who would not prefer him to clear signs or their Creator and knew his power was limited to worldly life.

TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r3.claim: The magicians' answer is rhetorically powerful, conveying profound wisdom and certainty in its wording, implications, and meaning.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r3.anchor: كلام بليغ في منطوقه بالغ في مفهومه بعيد في معناه رفيع في منزلته

TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r4.claim: The magicians had been awed by Pharaoh and worldly finery, even proclaiming victory by his might; after seeing truth's signs, they lost their awe of his power and worldly status and were freed from cowardice, flattery, caprice, and longing for worldly glitter.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r4.anchor: فما لبثوا دون أن ظهرت لهم آيات الحق فبهرت أبصارهم فطاحت عند ذلك ما كانوا يرون لفرعون من عزة وسلطان

TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r5.claim: The believers now attach themselves to truth and God's authority: they will what God wills, hope only in God, and fear only God.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r5.anchor: فلا يريدون إلا ما أراده الله ولا يرجون إلا الله ولا يخافون إلا الله عز اسمه

TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r6.claim: Pharaoh is oblivious to God, sees only himself as Egypt's lord with subjects, land, and armies, and imagines truth must submit to his falsehood and people's recognition of truth must await his permission.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r6.anchor: يرى أن الحق تبع باطله والحقيقة خاضعة مطيعة لدعواه فيتوقع أن لا تمس نفوس الناس

TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r8.claim: The believers regard Pharaoh's worldly wealth and status as a deceptive mirage; they face a choice between truth and falsehood, and people of certainty cannot prefer the mirage over truth.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r8.anchor: فقد خيروا بين الحق، والباطل والحقيقة والسراب، وحاشا أهل اليقين أن يشكوا في يقينهم

TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r9.claim: By saying they will not prefer Pharaoh, the magicians mean they will not prefer the broad worldly resources and gains he claimed to own, rather than merely his person.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r9.anchor: فليس مرادهم به إيثار شخص بما هو جسد إنساني ذو روح بل ما معه مما كان يدعيه أنه يملكه من الدنيا العريضه

SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r1.claim: The wāw may coordinate the relative pronoun with ما جاءنا: they will not prefer the tyrant over what came to them or over their Creator.
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r1.anchor: أن الواو عاطفة، عطفت هذا الموصول على " ما جاءنا " أي: لن نؤثرك على الذي جاءنا، ولا على الذي فطرنا

SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r2.claim: On the coordinate reading, they mention their Creator last as a progression from lesser to greater.
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r2.anchor: وإنما أخروا ذكر الباري تعالى لأنه من باب الترقي من الأدنى إلى الأعلى

SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r3.claim: Alternatively the wāw is an oath and the relative pronoun its object; the omitted answer means “by the Creator, we will not prefer you to the truth.”
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنها واو قسم، والموصول مقسم به. وجواب القسم محذوف أي: وحق الذي فطرنا لا نؤثرك على الحق

SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r4.claim: Even grammarians who allow a fronted oath answer do not accept لن نؤثرك as the answer here except in rare usage.
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r4.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون الجواب " لن نؤثرك " عند من يجوز تقديم الجواب

SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r5.claim: The clearer analysis makes ما relative (“what you will decide”); أنت قاض is its clause, with omitted object ـه permissible because the relative has accusative syntactic position.
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r5.anchor: أظهرهما: أنها موصولة بمعنى الذي، و " أنت قاض " صلتها والعائد محذوف، اي: قاضيه

SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats ما as a temporal verbal noun: decide your affair for as long as you are deciding.
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r6.anchor: والثاني: أنها مصدرية ظرفية، والتقدير: فاقض أمرك مدة ما أنت قاض. ذكر ذلك أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r7.claim: Some reject the verbal-noun analysis because ما cannot introduce a nominal clause; the author says this is not agreed and many grammarians permit it.
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r7.anchor: لأن: " ما " المصدرية لا توصل بالجملة الاسمية. وهذا المنع ليس مجمعا عليه

SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r8.speaker: ابن مالك
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r8.claim: Ibn Malik says nominal clauses after temporal ما are common, citing a poem; they are rarer when ما is non-temporal.
SAMIN-DURR:20:72/r8.anchor: ونقل ابن مالك أن ذلك يكثر إذا دلت " ما " على الظرفية

SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r1.claim: In one analysis, ما enables إن to govern a verb; الحياة الدنيا is an adverb of time, with the object of تقضي omitted (“your purpose/affair”).
SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أن تكون المهيئة لدخول " إن " على الفعل و " الحياة الدنيا " ظرف ل " تقضي "

SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r2.claim: Alternatively الحياة is an object by extension; Abu Haywa's passive تقضى raises الحياة as نائب فاعل, supporting this construction.
SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون " الحياة " مفعولا به على الاتساع، ويدل لذلك قراءة أبي حيوة " تقضى هذه الحياة "

SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r3.claim: If ما is a verbal noun and subject of إن, the predicate is the locative phrase: “your deciding is only in this worldly life,” meaning they have the afterlife.
SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r3.anchor: والثاني: أن تكون " ما " مصدرية هي اسم " إن " ، والخبر الظرف

SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa says that if a nominative reading of الحياة is transmitted, it would be إن's predicate with ما as a relative and an omitted object pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:20:72#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " فإن كان قد قريء بالرفع فهو خبر إن "

ASAD-NOTES:20:72/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:72/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:72/r1.claim: The magicians refuse to prefer Pharaoh over clear proofs and their Creator, accepting that Pharaoh can decree only for this worldly life.
ASAD-NOTES:20:72/r1.anchor: Never shall we prefer thee to all the evidence of the truth that has come unto us, nor to Him who has brought us into being! Decree, then, whatever thou art going to decree

ASAD-NOTES:20:72#n55/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:72#n55/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:72#n55/r1.claim: The verb qada can mean either “decree” or “end”; the magicians may mean Pharaoh can end only their worldly life.
ASAD-NOTES:20:72#n55/r1.anchor: the verb qada signifies, among other meanings, "he decreed" as well as "he ended [something]"

NASHR:v2p176/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p176/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p176/r1.claim: The remaining 566 possessive yāʾs in this chapter are agreed to have sukūn; the stated disagreements apply only in connected recitation.
NASHR:v2p176/r1.anchor: (واتفقوا) على إسكان ما بقي من هذا الفصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r5.claim: The magicians refuse to choose Pharaoh, his party, and safety from his torture over the clear proofs they received and knew to be true; their words belittle his threat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r5.anchor: قالوا لن نؤثرك أي لن نختار اتباعك وكوننا من حزبك وسلامتنا من عذابك على ما جاءنا من البينات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r6.claim: They say the proofs came to them because they knew magic better than others and recognized Moses’ sign was no magic; others relied on their expertise, and the proofs especially benefited them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r6.anchor: وفي نسبة المجيء إليهم وإن كانت البينات جاءت لهم ولغيرهم لأنهم كانوا أعرف بالسحر من غيرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r7.claim: The waw coordinates with “what came to us”; some instead take it as an oath whose response is omitted, since لن rarely answers a negative oath.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r7.anchor: والواو في والذي فطرنا واو عطف على ما جاءنا أي وعلى الذي فطرنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r8.claim: By moving from the miracle to its creator, they invoke God’s power to break natural patterns and expose Pharaoh’s false divinity: he cannot create even a fly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r8.anchor: لما لاحت لهم حجة الله في المعجزة بدؤوا بها ثم ترقوا إلى القادر على خرق العادة وهو الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r9.claim: Another parsing treats the waw as an oath with an omitted response; لن نؤثرك cannot serve as that response except in rare poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: الواو للقسم وجوابه محذوف، ولا يكون لن نؤثرك جوابا لأنه لا يجاب في النفي بلن إلا في شاذ من الشعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r10.claim: ما is taken as a relative pronoun meaning “what you decree,” with its object-link omitted; the author notes that some grammarians allow masdariyya ما to join a nominal clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r10.anchor: وما موصولة بمعنى الذي وصلته أنت قاض والعائد محذوف أي ما أنت قاضيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r11.claim: هذه الحياة is accusative as an adverbial phrase; ما may be preparatory or masdariyya, meaning Pharaoh’s decree ends in earthly life, while the believers receive bliss and he receives punishment in the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r11.anchor: وانتصب هذه الحياة على الظرف وما مهيئة ويحتمل أن تكون مصدرية أي إن قضاءك كائن في هذه الحياة الدنيا لا في الآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r1.claim: The magicians say they will not choose Pharaoh in faith and submission over what God sent through Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r1.anchor: ( ﴿ قالوا ﴾ ( غير مكترثين بوعيده ( ﴿ لن نؤثرك ﴾ ( لن نختارك بالأيمان والأنقياد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r2.claim: The manifest signs are the miracles, including the staff, which came from God through Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r2.anchor: من الله تعالى على يد موسى عليه السلام ( من البينات ( من المعجزات الظاهرة التي اشتملت عليها العصا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r3.claim: They say the signs came ‘to us’ because they benefited from them and knew them directly and fully, without imitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r3.anchor: وإن عم لانهم المتفعون بذلك والعارفون به على أتم وجه من غير تقليد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r4.claim: The phrase ما جاءنا is a relative construction; its relative clause is what follows, with a concealed pronoun as its resumptive, though deletion of a prepositional phrase is also proposed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r4.anchor: وما موصولة وما بعدها صلتها والعائد الضمير المستتر في جاذ وقيل العائد محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r5.claim: Some take the implied antecedent of جاءنا to be Moses: ‘what Moses brought to us’; al-Ālūsī finds this strained, including the proposed deletion of that prepositional phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r5.anchor: وقيل العائد محذوف وضمير ( جاءنا ) لموسى عليه السلام أي على الذي جاءنا به موسى عليه السلام وفيه بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r6.claim: The one who originated us is also the creator of all the higher and lower realms.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r6.anchor: أي أبدعنا وأوجدنا وسائر العلويات والسفليات

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r7.claim: The creator phrase is coordinated with the signs but comes later because it expresses a rational, theoretical proof, whereas the signs were directly witnessed; it also gives the reason not to prefer Pharaoh, himself created by God.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r7.anchor: وتأخيره لأن ما في ضمنه إية عقلية نظرية وما شاهدوه إية حسية ظاهرة وايراده تعالى بعنوان الفاظرية لهم للاشعار بعلة الحكم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r8.claim: Calling God their creator repudiates Pharaoh’s claim to divinity, since Pharaoh too is one of God’s created beings.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r8.anchor: فان ابدعه تعالى لهم وكون فرعون من جملة مبدعاته سبحانه مما يوجب عدم ايثارهم إياه عليه عز وجل وفيه تكذيب للعين في دعواه الربوبية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r9.claim: Another analysis makes the wāw an oath and omits its answer, understood from their words ‘we will not prefer you’; Abū Ḥayyān disallows the following clause as answer because an oath is not answered with لن except rarely in poetry.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r9.anchor: وقيل : الواو للقسم وجوابه محذوف لدلالة المذكور عليه أي وحق الذي فطرنا لن نؤثرك الخ ولا مساغ لكون المذكور جوابا عند من يجوز تقديم الجواب أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r10.claim: Their reply answers Pharaoh’s threat to cut them apart: do or decree what you intend; the imperative is not meant literally as a command.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r10.anchor: وقولهم : هذا جواب لتوبيخ اللعين بقوله : آمنتم الخ وقوله تعالى ( فاقض ما أنت قاض ( جواب عن تهديده بقوله : لأقطعن الخ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r11.claim: Qaḍāʾ can mean bringing something into existence, as in ‘He made them seven heavens,’ or its familiar sense of judging; the relative phrase has an omitted antecedent.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232#2/r11.anchor: فالقضاء أما بمعنى الايجاد الابداعي كما في قوله تعالى ( فقضاهن سبع سموات ) وأما بمعناه المعروف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r1.claim: The continuation explains why they are undeterred by the command to do as he pleases: Pharaoh’s power is confined to worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r1.anchor: مع ما بعده تعليل لعدم المبالاة المستفد مما سبق من الأمر بالفضاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r2.claim: On the main parse, ما is restrictive, هذه الحياة is an adverbial accusative, and the object is omitted: he can only do or judge what he wishes in this life.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r2.anchor: وماكافة و ( هذه الحياة ) منصوب محلا على الظرفية لتقضى والقضاء على ما أمر ومفعوله محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r3.claim: The believers have no desire for worldly pleasure and no fear of worldly punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r3.anchor: فحسب ومالنا من رغبة في عذبها ولارهبة من عذابها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r4.claim: Alternatively, ما is a verbal noun particle, so its clause becomes the subject of إن and ‘this worldly life’ is its predicate: Pharaoh’s action is confined to this life.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r4.anchor: وجوز أن تكون ما مصدرية فهى وما في حيزها في تأويل مصدر اسم أن وخبرها ( هذه الحياة ) أي أن قضاءك كائن في هذه الحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r5.claim: A further parse treats the verb as intransitive, with no omitted object.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r5.anchor: وجوز أن ينزل الفعل في منزلة اللازم فلا حذف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r6.speaker: أبو حياة وابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r6.claim: Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read إنما تقضى in the passive, with هذه الحياة nominative as the agent-like subject after the adverb is construed as an object.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو حياة وابن أبي عبلة ( انما تقضى ) بالبناء للمفعول ( هذه الحياة ) بالرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287#2/r3.claim: The magicians’ refusal expresses the high aspiration produced by certainty: eternal spiritual bliss outweighs worldly happiness, bodily suffering, immediate pleasure, and physical pain.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287#2/r3.anchor: كلام صادر من عظم الهمة الحاصل للنفس بقوة اليقين

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r1.claim: They will not choose Pharaoh over the truth and signs that came through Moses; the pronoun may refer to what came to us.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r1.anchor: لن نختارك. { على ما جاءنا } موسى به، ويجوز أن يكون

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r2.claim: The bayyināt are the clear miracles.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r2.anchor: { من البينت } المعجزات الواضحات. { والذى فطرنا }

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r3.claim: The phrase may be coordinated with what came to them or be an oath by their Creator.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r3.anchor: عطف على ما جاءنا أو قسم. { فاقض ما أنت قاض }

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r4.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do or decree whatever he will.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r4.anchor: ما أنت قاضيه أي صانعه أو حاكم به.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r5.claim: Pharaoh can only do what he wishes or judge as he sees fit in this life; that limits his power and prepares the contrast with the hereafter.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r5.anchor: إنما تصنع ما تهواه، أو تحكم ما تراه في هذه الدنيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r6.claim: A reading with the active form taqḍī is likened to the passive form in ṣīma yawm al-jumʿa.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:72/r6.anchor: وقرىء { تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا } كقولك: صيم يوم الجمعة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r1.speaker: السحرة
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r1.claim: The sorcerers refuse to follow Pharaoh to escape his temporary punishment, choosing instead the clear signs Moses brought, which they witnessed and knew could not be matched.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r1.anchor: على ما جاءنا } به موسى عليه السلام { من البينات } التي عايناها وعلمنا أنه لا يقدر أحد على مضاهاتها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r2.claim: Having inferred the Creator from the miraculous act, they name Him directly as the one who originated them, affirming His lordship over them, Pharaoh, and everyone else, and Pharaoh's helplessness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r2.anchor: ترقوا إلى ذكره بعد معرفته بفعله , إشارة إلى علي قدره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r3.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do what he judges, recognizing that whatever he can do to them is only by God's permission.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r3.anchor: علما بأن ما فعله فهو بإذن الله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r4.claim: Pharaoh's rule reaches only the body and this short worldly life; the spirit faces lasting divine reward or punishment, so they fear only the One who judges beyond bodily death.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r4.anchor: إنما حكمك في مدتها على الجسد خاصة , فهي ساعة تعقب راحة , ةنحن لانخاف إلاممن يحكم على الروح

BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r5.claim: The preposition في is omitted before this worldly life; even if Pharaoh's jurisdiction lasted to the world's end, it would remain fleeting beside God's enduring judgment.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r5.anchor: ولعلمه أسقطوا الجار تنزلا إلى أن حكمه لو فرض أنه يمتد إلى آخر الدنيا لكان أهلا لأن لا يخشى

BURSEVI:v5p312/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p312/r1.claim: The magicians answer Pharaoh without being daunted by his threat.

BURSEVI:v5p312/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p312/r2.claim: Kashifi portrays the magicians as intoxicated by divine attraction and overcome by the lights of repeated divine kindness; his Persian verse describes abandoning transient things for the Everlasting.
BURSEVI:v5p312/r2.anchor: ساحران ون ازجام جذبه حقانى مست شده بودند واز انوار تواتر ملاطفات ربانى كه بردل ايشان تافته بود

BURSEVI:v5p312/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p312/r3.claim: They will not choose Pharaoh in faith and obedience over the guidance God sent through Moses.
BURSEVI:v5p312/r3.anchor: لن نختارك بالإيمان والاتباع {على ما جاءنا} من الله على يد موسى

BURSEVI:v5p312/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p312/r4.claim: The clear signs are manifest miracles whose truth admits no doubt; they reason that if the display were magic, their ropes and staffs would still be present.
BURSEVI:v5p312/r4.anchor: من المعجزات الظاهرة التي لا شبهة في حقيتها وكان من استدلالهم أنهم قالوا : لو كان هذا سحرا فأين حبالنا

BURSEVI:v5p312/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p312/r5.claim: Seeing the signs revealed lights of the divine Essence and attributes, making immense trials seem slight; whoever prefers God over all else bears hardship for Him easily.
BURSEVI:v5p312/r5.anchor: القوم شاهدوا في رؤية الآيات أنوار الذات والصفات فهان عليهم عظائم البليات ومن آثر الله على الأشياء

BURSEVI:v5p312/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312/r6.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v5p312/r6.claim: A great Sufi says knowing that God is the one testing you eases the pain of affliction.
BURSEVI:v5p312/r6.anchor: وقد قال بعض الكبار ليخفف ألم البلاء عنك علمك أن الله هو المبلى

BURSEVI:v5p312/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p312/r7.claim: The One who created us means the creator of them and all creatures; this rational, reflective proof is placed after the sensory sign they witnessed.
BURSEVI:v5p312/r7.anchor: أي : خلقنا وسائر المخلوقات عطف على ما جاءنا وتأخيره لأن ما في ضمنه آية عقلية نظرية

BURSEVI:v5p312/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p312/r8.claim: One view takes the phrase as an oath with an omitted answer: by the Creator, they will not prefer Pharaoh; the construction with lan is exceptional.
BURSEVI:v5p312/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم هو قسم محذوف الجواب لدلالة المذكور عليه أي : وحق الذي فطرنا لا نؤثرك فإن القسم لايجاب بلن إلا على شذوذ

BURSEVI:v5p312/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312/r9.speaker: التفسير الفارسي
BURSEVI:v5p312/r9.claim: The Persian commentary renders the phrase as an oath: they swear by God who created them.
BURSEVI:v5p312/r9.anchor: وفي "التفسير الفارسي" : (وسوكنده ميخوريم بخدايى كه مارا آفريد).

BURSEVI:v5p312/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312/r10.speaker: التأويلات
BURSEVI:v5p312/r10.claim: The inward commentary reads the phrase as the One who formed them upon Islam’s primordial nature, which makes preferring Pharaoh over God impossible.
BURSEVI:v5p312/r10.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : أي : بالذي فطرنا على فطرة الإسلام والتعرض للفاطرية

BURSEVI:v5p312/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p312/r11.claim: Their reply answers Pharaoh’s threat to cut off hands and feet and crucify them: he may do what he wishes or pass sentence by cutting and crucifying.
BURSEVI:v5p312/r11.anchor: جواب عن تهديده بقوله لأقطعن أن فاصنع ما أنت صانعه أو احكم فينا ما أنت فيه حاكم من القطع والصلب

BURSEVI:v5p312/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312/r12.speaker: التأويلات
BURSEVI:v5p312/r12.claim: The inward reading takes their words as accepting the martyrdom God decreed for them from eternity.
BURSEVI:v5p312/r12.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : أي : فاحكم وأجر علينا ما قضى الله لنا في الأزل من الشهادة

BURSEVI:v5p312/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p312/r13.claim: Pharaoh can exercise his will only during their brief worldly lives; his power will soon pass, and they neither crave worldly pleasures nor fear worldly punishment.
BURSEVI:v5p312/r13.anchor: إنما تصنع ما تهواه أو تحكم بما تراه في هذه الحياة الدنيا ومدة حياتنا فحسب فسيزول أمرك وسلطانك عن قريب

BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan marvels that these former unbelievers believed instantly and did not hesitate to accept death for God; he contrasts them with people who study the Quran for sixty years yet sell their religion cheaply.
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r8.anchor: قال الحسن : سبحان الله لقوم كفارهم أشد الكافرين كفرا ثبت في قلوبهم الإيمان طرفة عين فلم يتعاظم

BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r9.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r9.claim: Saadi’s couplet laments the scholar who sells learning for bread and the rational person who trades away faith.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r1.claim: The magicians dismiss Pharaoh’s threat because faith has given them conviction; converts to the prophets similarly turn quickly from hardened unbelief to the wisdom and firmness of faith, as ʿUmar did.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r1.anchor: أظهروا استخفافهم بوعيده وبتعذيبه ، إذ أصبحوا أهل إيمان ويقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r2.claim: الإيثار means preferring one thing over another, as in the brothers’ statement to Joseph.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r2.anchor: والإيثار : التفضيل . وتقدم في قوله تعالى : { لقد آثرك الله علينا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r3.claim: The comparison with the clear signs requires an omitted complement: they will not prefer Pharaoh’s obedience or religion to the signs proving that God must be obeyed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r3.anchor: والتفضيل بين فرعون وما جاءهم من البينات مقتض حذف مضاف يناسب المقابلة بالبينات ، أي لن نؤثر طاعتك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r4.claim: The coordinated phrase means they will not prefer Pharaoh in divinity over their Creator; fāṭir, the one who created them, deserves preference.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r4.anchor: وبذلك يلتئم عطف { والذي فطرنا } ، أي لا نؤثرك في الربوبية على الذي فطرنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r5.claim: They place the signs before the Creator because those signs prove He wants them to believe in Moses and reject worship of others; the order also indirectly invites Pharaoh to believe in God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r5.anchor: وأخر { الذي فطرنا عن ما جاءنا من البينات } لأن البينات دليل على أن الذي خلقهم أراد منهم الإيمان بموسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r6.claim: The imperative is used to express indifference: whether Pharaoh carries out all, part, or none of his threat makes no difference to them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r6.anchor: وصيغة الأمر في قوله { فاقضض ما أنت قاض } مستعملة في التسوية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r7.claim: Here القضاء means to execute or carry out the threatened punishment, namely cutting off hands and feet and crucifying them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r7.anchor: فافعل ما أنت فاعل ( والقضاء هنا التنفيذ والإنجاز )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r8.claim: الحياة is accusative as a substitute for a ظرف; what is intended is the duration of this life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r8.anchor: وانتصب { هذه الحياة } على النيابة عن المفعول فيه ، لأن المراد بالحياة مدتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r9.claim: إنما restricts Pharaoh’s power to judgment in this worldly life; it does not extend to judgment in the hereafter, making the restriction absolute.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r9.anchor: والقصر المستفاد من ( إنما ) قصر موصوف على صفة ، أي إنك مقصور على القضاء في هذه الحياة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r10.claim: Pharaoh’s punishment cannot extend beyond worldly life, whereas the believers hope for their Lord’s everlasting reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p266/r10.anchor: فإن عذابك لا يتجاوز هذه الحياة ونحن نرجو من ربنا الجزاء الخالد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r1.claim: The sorcerers will not prefer Pharaoh, nor safety from him, over God's proofs and the Creator who made them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r1.anchor: لن نؤثرك أي نفضلك ونفضل السلامة منك على ما رأينا من حجة الله تعالى وآياته البينات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r2.claim: One group takes the waw as a conjunction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r2.anchor: على قول جماعة أن الواو في قوله والذي فطرنا عاطفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r3.claim: Another group takes the waw as an oath.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r4.claim: Faṭaranā means created and originated us.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r5.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do as he pleases: his authority ends with worldly life, while they will have bliss and he punishment afterward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r5.anchor: فافعل يا فرعون ما شئت وإنما قضاؤك في هذه الحياة الدنيا والآخرة من وراء ذلك لنا بالنعيم ولك بالعذاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r6.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r6.claim: One group says Pharaoh crucified the sorcerers as threatened; by God's mercy they became martyrs after being sorcerers that morning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r6.anchor: فقالت طائفة صلبهم على الجذوع كما قال فأصبح القوم سحرة وأمسوا شهداء بلطف الله لهم وبرحمته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r7.claim: Another group says Pharaoh did not execute them, since God had promised victory to Moses and his companions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة إن فرعون لم يفعل ذلك وقد كان الله تعالى وعد موسى أنه ومن معه الغالبون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r8.claim: Both accounts are possible; execution does not contradict Moses's victory except under an apparent general reading that can be resolved.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r8.anchor: وهذا كله محتمل وصلب السحرة وقطعهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r1.claim: The clear proofs brought by Moses are the staff and the hand.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r2.claim: The sorcerers say the proofs came to them because they knew magic and its tricks best, and recognized Moses' signs were not magic; this made the truth clearer to others too.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r2.anchor: وقد علموا أن ما جاء به موسى ليس بسحر كان ذلك في حق غيرهم أبين وأوضح وكانوا هم لمعرفته أخص

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r3.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r3.claim: One parsing coordinates the Creator with the proofs: they will not prefer Pharaoh over the proofs or over their Creator.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r3.anchor: أحدهما أن المعنى لن نؤثرك على ماجاءنا من البينات وعلى الذي فطرنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r4.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r4.claim: The second parsing treats the phrase as an oath: by the One who created us.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r4.anchor: والثاني أنه قسم تقديره وحق الذي فطرنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r5.claim: The command means: do what you are going to do; the root sense of judging is firm execution.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r5.anchor: أي فاصنع ما أنت صانع واصل القضاء عمل باحكام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r6.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r6.claim: Al-Farra says innamā is one particle, which is why al-ḥayāta is accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r6.anchor: قال الفراء إنما حرف واحد فلهذا نصب الحياة الدنيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r7.claim: A reader may put al-ḥayātu in the nominative by treating mā as a relative pronoun: what you rule on is this worldly life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r7.anchor: ولو قرأ قارىء برفع الحياة لجاز على أن يجعل ما في مذهب الذي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r8.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة وأبو المتوكل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r8.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla and Abu al-Mutawakkil read the verb passively and put al-ḥayātu in the nominative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة وأبو المتوكل إنما تقضى بضم التاء على مالم يسم فاعله الحياة برفع التاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r9.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r9.claim: The commentators explain that Pharaoh's authority and dominion end with this world and do not extend into the hereafter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p307/r9.anchor: قال المفسرون والمعنى إنما سلطانك وملكك في هذه الدنيا لا في الآخرة

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r1.claim: The relative pronoun may be accusative, coordinated with what came to them, or genitive as the object of an oath.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r1.anchor: (والذي فطرنا) محل (الذي) من الإعراب يحتمل النصب عطفا

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r3.claim: الحياة is accusative as the object of تقضي; alternatively it is accusative after an omitted preposition في, or nominative as the predicate after هذه.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r3.anchor: الحياة نصب ب (تقضي) وقيل: تقديره: في الحياة الدنيا، فلما سقطت الخافضة نصب، ويحتمل الرفع على (هذه)

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r10.claim: Having understood the threat, the magicians chose obedience to God and the next life over worldly life and its comforts.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r10.anchor: فلما سمع المستبصرون وعيده لهم آثروا طاعة الله والدار الآخرة على الدنيا ونعيمها

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r11.claim: The clear proofs are either arguments demonstrating divine unity or the hand and staff signs.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r11.anchor: على ما جاءنا من البينات قيل: الحجج الدالة على التوحيد، وقيل: اليد والعصا

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r12.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r12.claim: Abu Ali explains the phrase as saying they would not prefer Pharaoh over their creator.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r12.anchor: قيل: معناه لن نؤثرك على الذي فطرنا، أي: خلقنا، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r13.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is an oath: by God, they would not prefer Pharaoh over the proofs and truth.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r13.anchor: وقيل: إنه قسم، أي: لن نؤثرك والله على ما جاءنا من البينات وما ظهر من الحق

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r14.claim: The phrase means do or judge whatever you wish, completely and decisively; it expresses submission, not an actual command, since they would not abandon God’s religion.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r14.anchor: احكم ما أنت حاكم، وليس هذا بأمر؛ وإنما هو استسلام

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r15.claim: Pharaoh has authority only in this world, not in the next.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r15.anchor: يعني إنما تملك الأمر والحكم في الدنيا، وليس لك سلطان إلا هاهنا دون الدار الآخرة

JISHUMI:v7p4702/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r13.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r13.claim: Al-Hasan marvels that faith settled so firmly in the magicians that Pharaoh’s threat did not deter them, contrasting them with people who trade religion cheaply after decades with the Quran.
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r13.anchor: وكان الحسن يقول: سبحان الله لقوم آمنوا فثبت في قلوبهم الإيمان حتى لم يتعاظم عندهم وعيد فرعون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r1.claim: والذي فطرنا can coordinate with ما جاءنا or function as an oath.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r1.anchor: { والذي فطرنا } عطف على ما جاءنا أو قسم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r2.claim: A reading is recorded with قالوا لن نؤثرك على; the usual reading treats الحياة الدنيا as an adverbial expression and its syntax allows it to be construed like an object.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r2.anchor: قرىء { قالوا لن نؤثرك على } ووجهها أن الحياة في القراءة المشهورة منتصبة على الظرف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r3.claim: A report says there were seventy-two magicians, two Copts and the rest Israelites, and that Pharaoh had forced them to learn sorcery.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r3.anchor: وروي : أن السحرة يعني رؤسهم كانوا اثنين وسبعين : الاثنان من القبط

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r4.claim: A report says the magicians asked Pharaoh to show them Mūsā asleep; seeing his staff guard him, they concluded it was not a magician's trick because sorcery fails while a magician sleeps.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r4.anchor: وروي : أنهم قالوا لفرعون : أرنا موسى نائما ففعل ، فوجدوه تحرسه عصاه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r7.claim: The three preceding verses are either a quotation of the magicians' speech or God's account rather than a quotation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r7.anchor: قيل في هذه الآيات الثلاث : هي حكاية قولهم . وقيل : خبر من الله لا على وجه الحكاية

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r1.claim: A report says Pharaoh's wife asked who had won; hearing Moses and Aaron, she believed. Pharaoh prepared a great stone to crush her, but God took her soul first.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r1.anchor: وقيل إن امرأة فرعون كانت تسأل : من غلب ؟ فقيل لها : موسى وهارون . فقالت : آمنت برب موسى وهارون

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r2.claim: “And the One who created us” may be an oath, or it may mean “nor [will we prefer you] over the One who created us.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r2.anchor: والذي فطرنا } فيه وجهان : أحدهما : أنه قسم . الثاني : بمعنى [ ولا ] على الذي فطرنا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r3.claim: The magicians tell Pharaoh to do whatever he will do.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r4.claim: Alternatively, they tell him to judge whatever he will judge.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r5.claim: One possible sense is that this worldly life alone passes away, while the afterlife remains.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r5.anchor: إن التي تنقضي وتذهب هذه الحياة الدنيا , وتبقى الآخرة

MUQATIL:20:72-73/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:72-73/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:72-73/r1.claim: The magicians refuse to choose Pharaoh over the signs, meaning the hand and staff, or their Creator; they tell him to judge them by cutting and crucifixion, since he rules only this life.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r1.claim: Lan nuʾthiraka means we will not choose or prefer you.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r2.claim: The clear proofs are decisive signs that show Moses is truthful.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r3.claim: The phrase may coordinate with what came to them, so they will not prefer Pharaoh over revelation or their Creator; alternatively, it is an oath with the response lan nuʾthiraka placed before it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r3.anchor: عطف على ما جاءنا أي لن نختارك على الذي جاءنا ولا على الذي خلقنا أو قسم وجوابه لن يؤثر مقدم على القسم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r4.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do whatever he will, including killing or persecuting them; alternatively, qāḍin means decide or judge. The cited line قضاهما is glossed as making or completing.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r4.anchor: ﴿ فاقض ما أنت قاض ﴾ فاصنع ما أنت صانع من القتل والطلب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r5.claim: The quoted poetic word قضاهما can mean he made or completed them, supporting the sense of doing what one intends.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r5.anchor: وعليهما مسرودتان قضاهما أي صنعهما أو أحكم ما أنت حاكم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r6.claim: The phrase means in this worldly life; the words are an adverb of time, limiting Pharaoh's power over them to their lifetime.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#3/r6.anchor: أي في هذه الحياة الدنيا فانتصب على الظروف أي إنما تحكم فينا مدة حياتنا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r1.claim: The magicians say they will not choose or prefer Pharaoh.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r1.anchor: { قالوا } يعني السحرة { لن نؤثرك } أي لن نختارك

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the clear proofs as certainty and knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد من اليقين والعلم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r3.speaker: عكرمة وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r3.claim: ʿIkrima and others say God showed the magicians their places in Paradise while they prostrated, prompting their refusal to prefer Pharaoh.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r3.anchor: وقال عكرمة وغيره: لما سجدوا أراهم الله في سجودهم منازلهم في الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r4.claim: A report says Pharaoh's wife believed after hearing Moses and Aaron had won, persisted despite his threat to crush her, and died before the stone struck her body.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r4.anchor: وكانت امرأة فرعون تسأل من غلب، فقيل لها: غلب موسى وهارون فقالت: آمنت برب موسى وهارون.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r5.claim: Another account says the head magician tested whether the serpent feared; learning it did not, he recognized the work of the Maker and believed.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r5.anchor: وقيل: قال مقدم السحرة لمن يثق به لما رأى من عصا موسى ما رأى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r6.claim: The phrase may coordinate the Creator with the clear proofs: they will not prefer Pharaoh over either.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r6.anchor: قيل: هو معطوف على { ما جاءنا من البينات } أي لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r7.claim: Alternatively it is an oath: by God, we will not prefer you.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو قسم أي والله لن نؤثرك

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r8.claim: The implied sense is whatever you are to judge; ما is relative, not a verbal noun joined to a verb.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r8.anchor: التقدير ما أنت قاضيه. وليست «ما» هاهنا التي تكون مع الفعل بمنزلة المصدر

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the challenge as do whatever you are going to do.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فاصنع ما أنت صانع

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r10.claim: Another explanation is decide whatever you will, including cutting them apart and crucifying them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r10.anchor: وقيل: فاحكم ما أنت حاكم أي من القطع والصلب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r11.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r11.claim: The yāʾ in قاض is elided in connected speech for the meeting of quiescent letters; Sībawayh prefers retaining it at pause.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r11.anchor: وحذفت الياء من قاض في الوصل لسكونها وسكون التنوين. واختار سيبويه إثباتها في الوقف

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r12.claim: Pharaoh's power to carry out his threat reaches only this worldly life.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r13.claim: The phrase can be an adverb meaning in the enjoyment or time of this life, with an object understood.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r13.anchor: وهي منصوبة على الظرف، والمعنى: إنما تقضي في متاع هذه الحياة الدنيا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r14.claim: Alternatively it means you judge the affairs of this life, with the phrase as object and ما restricting إن.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r14.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التقدير: إنما تقضي أمور هذه الحياة الدنيا، فتنتصب انتصاب المفعول

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r15.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r15.claim: Al-Farrāʾ permits nominative parsing by treating ما as a relative pronoun and deleting the object pronoun from تقضي.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r15.anchor: وأجاز الفراء الرفع على أن تجعل «ما» بمعنى الذي وتحذف الهاء من تقضي ورفعت «هذه الحياة الدنيا».

QASHANI:20:72-73/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:72-73/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:72-73/r1.claim: Their refusal reflects the soul's high aspiration, which certainty in the heart produces: worldly fortune, bodily hardship, fleeting pleasure, and sensory pain matter little beside enduring intellectual bliss.
QASHANI:20:72-73/r1.anchor: عظم الهمة الحاصلة للنفس بقوة اليقين، إذ قوة اليقين في القلب تورث النفس عظم الهمة

QASHANI:20:72-73/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:72-73/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:72-73/r2.claim: They dismiss Pharaoh's threat because it concerns only the present worldly life.
QASHANI:20:72-73/r2.anchor: استخفوا بها واستحقروها بقولهم: { إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا }

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r1.claim: Their answer to Pharaoh's threat shows full certainty in religious fundamentals: they will not prefer him over clear proofs, since worldly gains and harms cannot rival those of the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r1.anchor: بما يدل على حصول اليقين التام والبصيرة الكاملة لهم في أصول الدين

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r2.claim: One parse supplies an understood repeated على: they will not prefer Pharaoh over the proofs or over obeying and worshipping their Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r2.anchor: التقدير لن نؤثرك يا فرعون على ما جاءنا من البينات وعلى الذي فطرنا

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r3.claim: A second parse takes والذي فطرنا as genitive in an oath.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r3.anchor: الوجه الثاني : يجوز أن يكون خفضا على القسم

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r4.claim: Their words do not command Pharaoh to carry out his threat; they declare that it cannot turn them from faith or from practicing the truth they know.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r4.anchor: لا على معنى أنهم أمروه بذلك لكن أظهروا أن ذلك الوعيد لا يزيلهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r5.claim: An alternative reading has نقضي, 'we spend' this worldly life.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r5.anchor: وقرىء : ( نقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا ) ووجهها

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r6.claim: In the received reading, الحياة is an accusative of time, extended by treating the adverbial as an object, as in صمت يوم الجمعة صيم.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r6.anchor: الحياة في القراءة المشهورة منتصبة على الظرف فاتسع في الظرف باجرائه مجرى المفعول به

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r7.claim: Pharaoh's judgment reaches only this fleeting worldly life, whereas their aim is lasting afterlife happiness; reason favors enduring finite harm to gain eternal bliss.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r7.anchor: قضاءك وحكمك إنما يكون في هذه الحياة الدنيا وهي كيف كانت فانية

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r13.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r13.claim: Al-Hasan marvels that former unbelievers gained faith in an instant and accepted persecution, while some who accompany the Qur'an for sixty years later sell their religion cheaply.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r13.anchor: قال الحسن : سبحان الله القوم كفار وهم أشد الكافرين كفرا ثبت في قلوبهم الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r14.claim: Their speech turns from the threat and their steadfast response to the contrasting fates of believers and criminals at the Resurrection, beginning with the criminal's Hell in 20:74.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r14.anchor: ثم ختموا هذا الكلام بشرح أحوال المؤمنين وأحوال المجرمين في عرصة القيامة

TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r1.claim: The sorcerers refuse to prefer Pharaoh by following him and rejecting Moses despite the proofs of the truth of his message.
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r1.anchor: فنتبعك ونكذب من أجلك موسى {على ما جاءنا من البينات} [طه: 72] يعني من الحجج والأدلة على حقيقة ما دعاهم إليه موسى

TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r2.claim: Al-fāṭir here means the one who created us, namely God.

TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r3.claim: Alladhī faṭaranā may be genitive by coordination with mā jāʾanā or as an oath, meaning by God.
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r3.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون قوله: {والذي فطرنا} [طه: 72] خفضا على القسم، فيكون معنى الكلام: لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والله

TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r4.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do as he wishes, since his power to punish them extends only through this fleeting worldly life.

TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r5.claim: Al-ḥayāta al-dunyā is accusative as a time expression, and innamā is treated as one particle.
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r5.anchor: ونصب الحياة الدنيا على الوقت وجعلت إنما حرفا واحدا

TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r6.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r6.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says Pharaoh's authority exists only in this life and not after it.
TAB-FULL:v16p116#2/r6.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، {لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والذي فطرنا} [طه: 72] أي على الله على ما جاءنا

SULAMI:v1p446#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p446#3/r1.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v1p446#3/r1.claim: Dhu al-Nun says whoever prefers God to everything finds sacrifice in God's cause easy, having chosen what is precious and taken on a light burden.
SULAMI:v1p446#3/r1.anchor: قال ذو النون : من آثر الله على الأشياء هان عليه

SULAMI:v1p446#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p446#3/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p446#3/r2.claim: The magicians' declaration shows that what God disclosed to them made carrying burdens and meeting harm easy, because the vision they received was easy to bear.
SULAMI:v1p446#3/r2.anchor: قال الله : جاء كيسا على السحرة لن نؤثرك

TABATABAI:20:73#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh treats earthly life as the only human life, containing all happiness and misery; the magicians instead affirm an everlasting life beyond it.
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r1.anchor: وهو يرى أن ليس للإنسان إلا الحياة التي فيها وفيها سعادته وشقاؤه فإنهم يرون الأمر بالعكس من ذلك

TABATABAI:20:73#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r2.claim: Because the afterlife is eternal and earthly life is fleeting, they will not fear worldly loss if they gain there; this answers Pharaoh’s threat of death.
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r2.anchor: إذا ربحوا في الحياة الأخرى الخالدة، وذلك قولهم لفرعون

TABATABAI:20:73#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r3.claim: “The clear signs” alludes to several signs they witnessed: the staff became a serpent, swallowed the ropes and staffs, then returned to its former state.
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r3.anchor: تلويح إلى أنهم عدوا ما شاهدوه من أمر العصا آيات عديدة كصيرورتها ثعبانا وتلقفها الحبال والعصي ورجوعها ثانيا

TABATABAI:20:73#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r4.claim: A possible alternative takes min as partitive: they saw one sign and believed God had many others; the author considers this reading far-fetched.
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r4.anchor: آمنوا بأن لله آيات أخرى كثيرة ولا يخلو من بعد.

TABATABAI:20:73#2/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r11.claim: They first call God the one who created them because creation makes Him the source of every real good; compared with Him, all else is an illusion, grounding their choice over Pharaoh.
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r11.anchor: لأن كونه تعالى فاطرا لنا أي مخرجا لنا عن كتم العدم إلى الوجود ويتبعه انتهاء كل خير حقيقي إليه

AKHFASH:v2p444/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p444/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p444/r1.claim: The phrase means 'the One who created us': they will not choose Pharaoh over their Creator.

FARRA:v2p187/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p187/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p187/r1.claim: The magicians tell Pharaoh to do whatever he wishes.
FARRA:v2p187/r1.anchor: وقوله (فاقض ما أنت قاض) : افعل ما شئت.

FARRA:v2p187/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p187/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p187/r2.claim: Because إنما is one particle, الحياة is accusative; nominative is also possible if ما is relative: “what you decree is this worldly life.”
FARRA:v2p187/r2.anchor: إنما حرف واحد، لذلك نصبت (الحياة) ولو قرأ قارئ برفع (الحياة) لجاز

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#8/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#8/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#8/r1.claim: The tyrant's command or authority takes effect only in this worldly life.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#8/r1.anchor: إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا} أي إنما يجوز أمرك فيها.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the clear signs as certainty and knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد من اليقين والعلم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r2.claim: Muqatil identifies the clear signs as the hand and the staff.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r3.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r3.claim: Ikrima says that when the sorcerers prostrated, God showed them the places in Paradise where they would end up.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r3.anchor: وقال عكرمة: (هو أنهم حيث خروا سجدا أراهم الله في سجودهم منازلهم في الجنة التي إليها يصيرون)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r4.speaker: القاسم بن أبي بزة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r4.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bizza says that they saw Paradise, Hell, and their inhabitants’ rewards before raising their heads from prostration, then said they would not prefer Pharaoh.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r4.anchor: ونحو هذا قال القاسم بن أبي بزة (¬4): (ما رفعوا رؤوسهم حتى رأوا الجنة والنار، ورأوا ثواب أهلها عند

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r5.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r5.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj offer two parses: the phrase coordinates the Creator with God, or it is an oath.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r5.anchor: ذكر الفراء والزجاج فيه وجهين أحدهما: (لن نؤثرك على الله والذي خلقنا. والثاني: أنه قسم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وجميع المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas and all commentators gloss the challenge as “do whatever you are going to do.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس وجميع المفسرين: (فاصنع ما أنت صانع)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh’s rule and dominion extend only through this worldly life; he has no authority or share in the next.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p465/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد إنما سلطانك وملكك في هذه الدنيا، فأما في الآخرة فليس لك فيها حظ ولا سلطان)

BURHAN:v3p192/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p192/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p192/r1.claim: One view places the oath's answer at “a lesson for whoever fears”; in the magicians' “we will never prefer you,” an omitted element is recoverable from the preceding speech.

BURHAN:v3p317/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p317/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p317/r1.claim: The magicians' shift from addressing Pharaoh to speaking in the first person is an instance of iltifat; it works as an example only for scholars who do not require the referent to remain the same.
BURHAN:v3p317/r1.anchor: وهذا إنما يتمشى على قول من لم يشترط أن يكون المراد بالالتفات واحدا

NAHHAS:v3p49/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p49/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p49/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq parses الذي as genitive by coordination with ما: they will not prefer Pharaoh over the proofs or God who created them.
NAHHAS:v3p49/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق الذي في موضع خفض على العطف والمعنى لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات وعلى الله

NAHHAS:v3p49/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p49/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p49/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq also allows الذي to be genitive as an oath.
NAHHAS:v3p49/r2.anchor: قال ويجوز أن يكون في موضع خفض على القسم

NAHHAS:v3p49/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p49/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p49/r3.claim: The final yāʾ is dropped in connected speech because it meets the still tanwīn; dropping it in pause signals that connected form.
NAHHAS:v3p49/r3.anchor: بحذف الياء في الوصل لسكونها وسكون التنوين وتحذف في الوقف دلالة على أنها في الوصل بغير ياء

NAHHAS:v3p49/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p49/r4.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v3p49/r4.claim: Sībawayh prefers retaining the yāʾ in pause because the cause of the two still letters has ended.
NAHHAS:v3p49/r4.anchor: واختار سيبويه إثباتها في الوقف لأنه قد زالت علة التقاء الساكنين

NAHHAS:v3p49/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p49/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p49/r5.claim: هذه الحياة الدنيا is accusative as a temporal adverb; the sense is that Pharaoh rules only the enjoyment of this worldly life.
NAHHAS:v3p49/r5.anchor: إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا ) منصوبة على الظرف والمعنى إنما تقضي في متاع هذه الحياة الدنيا

NAHHAS:v3p49/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p49/r6.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p49/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows nominative if ما is treated as a relative pronoun.
NAHHAS:v3p49/r6.anchor: وأجاز الفراء الرفع على أن يجعل ما بمعنى الذي

ITQAN:v2p470/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p470/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p470/r1.claim: Ḥattā is a preposition like ilā, but it governs only an overt noun at an endpoint preceded by something divisible or contiguous.
ITQAN:v2p470/r1.anchor: فتنفرد حتى بأنها لا تجر إلا الظاهر وإلا الآخر المسبوق بذي إجزاء أو الملاقي له

ITQAN:v2p470/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p470/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p470/r2.claim: Ḥattā marks an action reaching its endpoint gradually and cannot mark the starting point.
ITQAN:v2p470/r2.anchor: وأنها لإفادة تقضي الفعل قبلها شيئا فشيئا وأنها لا يقابل بها ابتداء الغاية

ITQAN:v3p217/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p217/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p217/r1.claim: On whether rhetorical interrogatives retain the interrogative sense alongside another force or lose it entirely, the author favors retention; al-Tanūkhī’s account of laʿalla supports this.
ITQAN:v3p217/r1.anchor: هل يقال إن معنى الاستفهام في هذه الأشياء موجود وانضم إليه معنى آخر أو تجرد عن الاستفهام بالكلية

ITQAN:v3p217/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p217/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p217/r4.claim: Confirmatory questioning can either assert that the proposition is true or ask an addressee to acknowledge it; the second account is more apparent and is explicit in al-Īḍāḥ.
ITQAN:v3p217/r4.anchor: وفي كلام أهل الفن ما يقتضي الاحتمالين والثاني أظهر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p82/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p82/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p82/r1.claim: The excellence of nazm arises from grammatical meanings, their relations, and the purpose and placement of the words; no form is inherently excellent in every context.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p82/r1.anchor: بل ليس من فضل ومزية إلا بحسب الموضع ، وبحسب المعنى الذي تريد ، والغرض الذي تؤم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p82/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p82/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p82/r2.claim: Choosing and arranging grammatical meanings resembles selecting and placing dyes to create a distinctive image; poets differ in this judgment and arrangement.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p82/r2.anchor: كذلك حال الشاعر والشاعر في توخيهما معاني النحو ، ووجوهه التي علمت أنها محصول النظم .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p82/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p82/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p82/r3.claim: Some poems accumulate their effect across several lines, while a single masterful verse in other poems can reveal the poet's skill and command at once.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p82/r3.anchor: ومنه ما أنت ترى الحسن يهجم عليك منه دفعة ، ويأتيك منه ما يملأ العين ضربة ، حتى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p506#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p506#2/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p506#2/r6.claim: Qaḍāʾ can mean doing or carrying out an action.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p506#2/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن القضاء في القرآن على خمسة عشر وجها :

STUDYQURAN:20:71/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r1.speaker: K
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r1.claim: The sorcerers’ certainty in God made them see worldly trials and pleasures as fleeting and finite beside eternal felicity in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r1.anchor: The sorcerers reached such a high degree of certainty in God that they came to see the trials and pleasures of this life as merely passing

STUDYQURAN:20:71/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r3.claim: The passage is cross-referenced with 7:123–26 and, for verse 71, 26:49.
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r3.anchor: See commentary on 7:123–26; cf. also v. 71 with 26:49

TABRISI:20:71-72/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r3.claim: “By the One who created us” is genitive, coordinated with the preceding phrase.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r3.anchor: والذي فطرنا موضعه جر عطف على ما جاءنا

TABRISI:20:71-72/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r4.claim: One parse makes ما a verbal noun in a temporal adverbial construction: carry out your judgment for as long as you are judging.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r4.anchor: يجوز أن يكون ما مصدرية في تقدير الظرف أي فاقض القضاء مدة كونك قاضيا

TABRISI:20:71-72/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r5.claim: Alternatively, ما is the object of قاض, with its object pronoun omitted.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ما مفعوله أي فاقض ما أنت قاضيه فحذف الهاء

TABRISI:20:71-72/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r6.claim: The phrase may omit a genitive: either “the affairs of this worldly life” or “the duration of this worldly life”; هذه is an object in the first parse and temporal accusative in the second.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r6.anchor: حذف المضاف وتقديره إنما تقضي أمور هذه الحياة الدنيا ويجوز أن يكون تقديره إنما تقضي مدة هذه الحياة الدنيا

TABRISI:20:71-72/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r7.claim: The conjunction wāw may also be read as an oath particle.

TABRISI:20:71-74/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r14.claim: They will not prefer Pharaoh over the proofs of Moses’ truth and prophethood, including miracles beyond human power.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r14.anchor: لن نفضلك ولن نختارك على ما أتانا من الأدلة الدالة على صدق موسى وصحة نبوته

TABRISI:20:71-74/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r15.claim: One explanation takes this as an oath: they will not prefer Pharaoh over the proofs and the God who created them.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r15.anchor: وقيل: معناه لن نؤثرك والله الذي فطرنا على ما جاءنا من البينات

TABRISI:20:71-74/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r16.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do whatever he is going to do thoroughly and decisively; alternatively, to judge as he pleases.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r16.anchor: أي فاصنع ما أنت صانعه على إتمام وإحكام. وقيل: معناه فاحكم ما أنت حاكم

TABRISI:20:71-74/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r17.claim: This is not an order from them; it means that whatever he does, they will not abandon their faith.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r17.anchor: وليس هذا بأمر منهم ولكن معناه أي شيء صنعت فإنا لا نرجع عن الإيمان

TABRISI:20:71-74/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r18.claim: Pharaoh’s power and judgment extend only through worldly life, not the afterlife; alternatively, this worldly life alone will pass away, while the next life remains.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r18.anchor: إنما تصنع بسلطانك أو تحكم في هذه الحياة الدنيا دون الآخرة

THALABI:v6p253/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p253/r2.claim: The magicians answer Pharaoh that they will not choose him over the clear proofs they have witnessed.
THALABI:v6p253/r2.anchor: قالوا يعني السحرة لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات

THALABI:v6p253/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r3.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v6p253/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the clear proofs as the hand and the staff.

THALABI:v6p253/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r4.speaker: القاسم بن أبي برزة
THALABI:v6p253/r4.claim: Qasim reports that Pharaoh assembled seventy thousand magicians, whose ropes and staffs seemed to move; Moses' staff swallowed them, and the magicians prostrated after seeing Paradise, Hell, and their rewards. The same report recounts Pharaoh's wife persisting in faith after being shown her home in Paradise, whereupon her soul was taken and a stone cast on her lifeless body.
THALABI:v6p253/r4.anchor: عن القاسم بن أبي برزة قال: جمع فرعون سبعين ألف ساحر،

THALABI:v6p253/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p253/r5.claim: By the One who formed us means by the One who created us.
THALABI:v6p253/r5.anchor: والذي فطرنا يعني وعلى الذي خلقنا

THALABI:v6p253/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r6.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v6p253/r6.claim: Another explanation takes the phrase as an oath.
THALABI:v6p253/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو قسم فاقض ما أنت قاض

THALABI:v6p253/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p253/r7.claim: The command means to judge and do whatever Pharaoh will, including cutting off limbs and crucifying them.
THALABI:v6p253/r7.anchor: ما أنت حاكم، واصنع ما أنت صانع من القطع والصلب إنما تقضي

THALABI:v6p253/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p253/r8.claim: Pharaoh's power over them lasts only in this worldly life; he has no authority over them beyond it.
THALABI:v6p253/r8.anchor: إنما تملكنا في الدنيا ليس لك علينا سلطان إلا في الدنيا

THALABI:v6p253/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p253/r9.claim: The magicians ask God to forgive their sins and the magic Pharaoh compelled them to practice.
THALABI:v6p253/r9.anchor: إنا آمنا بربنا ليغفر لنا خطايانا وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر

THALABI:v6p253/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r10.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v6p253/r10.claim: Mujahid says the seventy-two magicians comprised two Egyptian leaders and seventy Israelites, whom Pharaoh had forced to learn magic.
THALABI:v6p253/r10.anchor: قال مقاتل: كانت السحرة اثنين وسبعين ساحرا، اثنان منهم من القبط

THALABI:v6p253/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r11.speaker: عبد العزيز بن أبان
THALABI:v6p253/r11.claim: Abd al-Aziz reports that the magicians asked Pharaoh to show them Moses asleep; seeing the staff guard him, they said this was not magic, since a magician's power ends during sleep, but Pharaoh still forced them to perform.
THALABI:v6p253/r11.anchor: عبد العزيز بن أبان: إن السحرة قالوا

THALABI:v6p253/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p253/r12.claim: God is better and more enduring than Pharaoh because Pharaoh is mortal and will perish.
THALABI:v6p253/r12.anchor: والله خير وأبقى منك لأنك فان هالك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r6.claim: The magicians will not choose Pharaoh's religion over the clear proofs, certainty, and guidance, nor over their Creator.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r6.anchor: لن نختار دينك { على ما جاءنا من البينات } اليقين والهدى { والذي فطرنا }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r7.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do as he pleases by cutting and crucifying them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r7.anchor: فاصنع ما أنت صانع من القطع والصلب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r8.claim: Pharaoh's authority and rule are confined to this worldly life.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r8.anchor: إنما سلطانك وملكك في هذه الحياة الدنيا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r10.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r10.claim: The magicians will not prefer Pharaoh over the proofs or over their Creator.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r10.anchor: قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r11.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r11.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do what he will, since his power to act is limited to worldly life.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r11.anchor: {فاقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا} [طه: 72] يقولون افعل في أمرنا ما أنت فاعل

QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r8.claim: They swear by the One who created them that they will not prefer Pharaoh to the clear proofs and the Creator.
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r8.anchor: أي بالله الذي فطرنا إنا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات

QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r10.claim: Because they recognized the ordeal as coming from God, they found it sweet and endured hardship without shrinking from Pharaoh's threats.
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r10.anchor: ورأوا ذلك من الله فاستعذبوا البلاء ، وتحملوا اللأواء

QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r11.claim: The magicians knew that worldly suffering ends, however long it lasts.
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r11.anchor: علموا أن البلاء في لدنيا ينقضي

QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r12.claim: For a person who knows God, the most important concern is that God forgive his errors.
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r12.anchor: أهم الأشياء - على من عرفه - مغفرته لخطاياه

QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r13.speaker: النبي
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r13.claim: The Prophet said that a veil sometimes comes over his heart and that he seeks God's forgiveness seventy times a day; Qushayri adduces this with scriptural examples of seeking forgiveness and divine pardon.
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r13.anchor: إنه ليغان على قلبي فأستغفر الله في اليوم سبعين مرة

FARRA:v2p186/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p186/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p186/r5.claim: والذي is genitive, coordinated with على: على الذي; it could also be genitive as an oath, as if they said لن نؤثرك والله.
FARRA:v2p186/r5.anchor: فالذي في موضع خفض: وعلى الذي. ولو أرادوا بقولهم (والذي فطرنا) القسم بها كانت خفضا

MAJAZ:v2p23/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p23/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p23/r3.claim: Iqḍi mā anta qāḍ means do and carry out whatever you intend; their decision has already been made. Abū Dhuʾayb’s poem uses qaḍā for making and finishing armor.
MAJAZ:v2p23/r3.anchor: «فاقض ما أنت قاض» (72) مجازه: اصنع ما أنت صانع وأنفذ ما أنت منفذ فقد قضى قضاؤك

MAJAZ:v2p23/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p23/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p23/r4.claim: Here taqḍī means this worldly life is passing or ending; elsewhere it resembles saying “I completed my journey.”
MAJAZ:v2p23/r4.anchor: «إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا» (72) وله موضع آخر فى معنى إنما تخلف هذه الحياة الدنيا

ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r2.claim: Alladhī is genitive in the sense that they will not prefer Pharaoh to God.
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r2.anchor: موضع الذي خفض، المعنى لن نؤثرك على الله

ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r3.claim: Alternatively, alladhī is genitive as an oath: they swear by God.
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r3.anchor: خفضا على القسم، ويكون المعنى لن نؤثرك

ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r4.claim: The command means, do what you are going to do.
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r4.anchor: أي: اصنع ما أنت صانع، قال أبو ذؤيب

ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r5.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r5.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb uses qaḍāhumā to mean that the two garments were made or fashioned.
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r5.anchor: قال أبو ذؤيب: وعليهما مسرودتان قضاهما

ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r6.claim: Al-ḥayāta al-dunyā is read in the accusative; a nominative is possible, though Zajjāj knows no one who read it.

ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r7.claim: With the nominative, the meaning is that what Pharaoh adjudicates is only the enjoyment of worldly life.
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r7.anchor: تأويله أن الذي تقضيه متاع الحياة الدنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r14.claim: The magicians say they will not choose Pharaoh over the clear proofs that came to them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r14.anchor: {قالوا} يعني السحرة: {لن نؤثرك} لن نختارك، {على ما جاءنا من البينات}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r15.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r15.claim: Muqatil says the clear proofs are the shining hand and the staff.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r16.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r16.claim: Another explanation says their proof was that, if Moses' act were magic, their ropes and staffs would still be there.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r16.anchor: وقيل: كان استدلالهم أنهم قالوا لو كان هذا سحرا فأين حبالنا وعصينا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r17.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r17.claim: A further gloss understands the clear proofs as clarification and knowledge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r17.anchor: وقيل: {من البينات} يعني من التبيين والعلم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r18.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r18.speaker: القاسم بن أبي بزة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r18.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza relates that the magicians kept their heads down after prostrating until they saw Paradise, Hell, and their own places in Paradise; then they spoke of the proofs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r18.anchor: حكي عن القاسم بن أبي بزة أنه قال: إنهم لما ألقوا سجدا ما رفعوا رءوسهم حتى رأوا الجنة والنار، ورأوا ثواب أهلها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r19.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r19.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r19.claim: The phrase means they would not prefer Pharaoh over God, who created them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r19.anchor: {والذي فطرنا} أي: لن نؤثرك على الله الذي فطرنا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r20.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r20.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r20.claim: Another analysis takes the words as an oath.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r21.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r21.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r21.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do whatever he is going to do.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r21.anchor: {فاقض ما أنت قاض} أي: فاصنع ما أنت صانع،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r22.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r22.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r22.claim: Pharaoh's power and judgment last only in worldly life and will soon pass away.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r22.anchor: {إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا} أي: أمرك وسلطانك في الدنيا وسيزول عن قريب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r2.claim: The sorcerers' lives became negligible to them for God; they refuse to choose Pharaoh over the guidance and certainty they have received.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r2.anchor: فلما صال عليهم بذلك وتوعدهم، هانت عليهم أنفسهم في الله عز وجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r3.claim: The phrase “by the One who originated us” can either be an oath or be grammatically coordinated with “the proofs.”
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r3.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون قسما، ويحتمل أن يكون معطوفا على البينات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r4.claim: They will not prefer Pharaoh to their Creator, who brought them from nothing and first formed them from clay; He alone deserves worship and submission.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r4.anchor: لا (5) نختارك على فاطرنا وخالقنا الذي أنشأنا من العدم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r5.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do whatever he wishes and whatever lies within his power.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r5.anchor: أي: فافعل ما شئت وما وصلت إليه يدك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r6.claim: Pharaoh's authority reaches only this transient life; the sorcerers desire the everlasting abode.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r6.anchor: أي: إنما لك تسلط في هذه الدار، وهي دار الزوال ونحن قد رغبنا في دار القرار

ITQAN:v3p229/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p229/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p229/r4.claim: Some give this as a shift from address to first-person speech, but it fails because the intended speakers are not one referent.
ITQAN:v3p229/r4.anchor: وهذا المثال لا يصح لأن شرط الالتفات أن يكون المراد به واحدا
